title: Spare slot harvest lab — weekly scrub (Apr 6 2027)
content:
TL;DR:
- Running the Spare Slot Harvest experiment (slot-harvester-v2) across three regions this week. Early wins: small uplift in effective capacity (measured as completed tokens/min per physical GPU) in us-west and eu-central when spare slots are opportunistically used for low-priority caching and precomputations.
- Incident: Apr 3 04:12 UTC preemption cascade in ap-southeast caused a ~12min P90 latency increase on hosted inference — root cause traced to provider maintenance + our backoff/reallocation policy not firing fast enough.
- Action items focused on: quick scheduler tweaks, telemetry additions, and a canary rollout of the new backoff policy (allocator v0.23).

Notes from the weekly sync (2027-04-06, 09:30 PT) — attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Rina, Jonah, SRE on-call (Maya).
- Objective recap: prove that harvesting <5% spare slots for non-critical work can reduce billable token cost per throughput by ~3–6% without affecting latency SLOs. Keep customer-visible latency regressions <0.5% at P95.
- Experiment shape: run slot-harvester-v2 as a best-effort consumer tagged "harvest-low" with a soft preemption budget in each region. Track: preemptions/min, slot-availability delta, cold-start rate, cache-hit % for prefix caches, and customer tail latency.

This week's observations:
1) us-west-2
   - Spare slot allocation: target 4% (configured) — measured ~3.8% average across peak window (08:00–12:00 PT).
   - Effective throughput: +4.1% tokens/min when harvester tasks ran at <60s avg runtime.
   - No SLO violations. Preemption rate for harvested tasks ~0.9 preemptions/hour.
   - Notes: need to tighten memory ceilings for harvested tasks; saw occasional oom in containerized precompute job.

2) eu-central-1
   - Spare slot allocation: target 5% — measured 5.4% (slightly higher due to under-provisioning for dedicated customers).
   - Throughput uplift: +3.3% tokens/min. Cache warmups from harvested precomputations cut upstream model cold-starts by ~7s on median for targeted routes.
   - Anomaly: one harvested job leaked a small KV cache (observed by increased host mem used across pool). Root cause: exploit of old library path; patch applied.

3) ap-southeast-1 (incident region)
   - Timeline: Apr 3 03:58–04:12 UTC — cloud provider scheduled maintenance + host rotation. Our harvester tasks were preempted, but due to a race in our reallocation circuit the allocator attempted to spin up replacements in the same batch of hosts that were being drained. Result: a short amplification of preemptions and a spotty increase in latency on customer traffic.
   - Impact: ~12 minutes of elevated P90 (from 240ms to 365ms) affecting internal latency SLO; no customer billing anomalies.
   - Root cause: insufficient early-detection signal for host draining. Our agent would only mark host "draining" after the first preemption event; provider emits maintenance notice earlier.
   - Mitigation already applied: add provider-maintenance webhook ingestion to allocator; bump reallocation backoff multiplier (x2.5 -> x3.5) for harvested tasks during detected host-drain windows.

Capacity planning and numbers:
- Target global buffer: 6% spare slots (goal to sustain 99.9% of peak without preemption wobble). Currently configured per-region: us-west-2=4%, eu-central-1=5%, ap-southeast-1=6.5% (ramped after incident).
- Projection for next 30 days (based on rolling 7d usage): expected peak growth +9% tokens/day on hosted API. Recommendation: pre-provision an extra 8 slot-equivalents in west/eu pools during predicted spikes (concerted marketing campaign on Apr 17 likely to increase traffic).

Runbook / automation notes:
- New play: on provider maintenance webhook, auto-drain harvested workloads first, then increase autoscaler aggressiveness for dedicated pools.
- Added two alerts:
  1) "harvest-preemptor-surge" — fires when harvested task preemption rate > 2.5x baseline for 3m.
  2) "host-drain-radar" — fires when provider maintenance webhook is received + host draining count > 1% of pool.
- SLO guard: when "host-drain-radar" triggers, harvested tasks get immediate soft-suspend and we shift backlog into aux-cache pipeline for later execution.

Engineering action items (owners + ETA):
- Miguel: merge allocator PR that ingests provider maintenance webhooks and exposes "drain_predicted" to policy engine. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/218 — ETA 2027-04-08.
- Rina: adjust harvester memory limits and add a small GC-friendly flag to the precompute container image. CI job updated; need one green canary deployment — ETA 2027-04-07.
- Jonah: rollout plan for backoff multiplier change in allocator config (canary in us-west, then eu, then ap). Coordinate with SRE — ETA start 2027-04-07, complete 2027-04-09.
- Maya (SRE): update runbook with the new alerts and test failure mode simulation in the chaos lab. Schedule a 30m drill. ETA 2027-04-13.
- Aisha (me): produce a one-pager for product + support explaining the experiment and the low risk to customers; for transparency in case of future brief SLO blips. ETA 2027-04-09.

Meeting notes (scrappy transcript highlights):
- Maya: "we had the telemetry but it was buried in control-plane logs — need an explicit signal."
- Miguel: "allocator should treat maintenance webhooks as high-fidelity signals, not heuristics."
- Rina: "harvested jobs must be memory-light and checkpoint frequently; precompute we did this week improved cache warms but we almost OOM'd."
- Jonah: "we should instrument a 'slot-hop' metric to surface when the allocator is aggressively bouncing the same request across hosts".

Open questions / discussion items:
- What is the long-term policy for harvested work? Keep at <5% globally, or make it region-adaptive with a max cap? Proposal: region-adaptive with hard cap at 6% and soft target 3–4% most regions.
- Economics: do we attribute harvested task cost to infra or to product? For now keep on infra budget while experiment lives. Need a finance sync if we scale.
- Feature request for product: an opt-out header for particularly latency-sensitive customers so their routes never hit reclaimed caches. Need product + docs input.

Quick wins for next sprint:
- Canary allocator change in us-west (Jonah)
- Harvester memory limit and GC flag (Rina)
- Add early webhook ingestion to CI staging (Miguel)
- SRE chaos drill (Maya)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Follow up with provider contacts to confirm maintenance notice lead time (APAC region).
- Add metric: "harvest_candidate_hit_rate" to slice by route and by customer tier.
- Keep default harvested job TTL small (30s) — long jobs cause too much churn.

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (2027-04-01 -> 2027-04-06 aggregated):
- avg spare slots observed (global): 4.7%
- tokens/min improvement when harvesting on: +3.7% global median
- harvested job preemption rate: 1.2 preemptions/hour (global)
- P95 latency delta during experiment windows: +0.8% (within acceptable threshold but ap-southeast incident bump noted)

If you have anything to add, drop notes in thread: slack:#infra-capacity or add to linked_artifacts list. Will re-run a deeper analysis after two full weeks of steady-state.

-- Aisha

[This is a working doc — expect edits and appendices (logs, small graphs) to be pasted here as we iterate.]
